title: Flowers of Crystal
build: TOSEC disc, Flowers of Crystal (1984)(4Mat).ssd (SHA-256 0f591a69...57d0), a 40-track DFS disc of eight BBC BASIC II programs and four files of machine code; each program analysed as CHAIN loads it at &1900, the two adventures' machine code where their sound programs load it

records.c: Line 3, `*KEY0`: defines f0 as `DELETE1,6`, `32220`, `32225`, `MODE7` and `RUN`, each ended by RETURN (|M). Nothing here presses it: the adventure part 1, chained by line 220, moves itself to &0E00 and then puts f0 in the keyboard buffer itself (its lines 5-6), so that back at BASIC's prompt the MOS types these commands, which delete the adventure's relocation lines and run it. The definition lives in the MOS's soft-key buffer at &0B00, which CHAIN does not touch.

Lines 20-60: MODE 7 and ON ERROR RUN; `*FX15,0` empties every input buffer; `*FX200,2` makes BREAK clear memory; VDU 6 and the cursor turned off (VDU 23;8202;0;0;0;); a pause of 0.8 seconds (INKEY(80)).

Line 70: S%=-3, the sound level the player gets by pressing the space bar straight away (level 1). Then `FLOWERS OF CRYSTAL` in double height on rows 6 and 7, printed three times through seven colour pairs: for a from 7 down to 1, letters in teletext colour a on a band in colour a-1 (CHR$(128+a-1), then new background, &9D), with an empty count of 100 between pairs and of 1000 after each pass. The last pair, a=1, leaves red letters on a band of white, the colour 128 giving none (live).
Line 75: `part  1` in double height under the title, rows 9 and 10, and a pause of two seconds (INKEY(200)).

Lines 80-150: `Select sound level 0-5`, one key read (GOSUB 200), then `< S >` and `Press the space bar when you are happy with the sound level.`, and from then on GOSUB 200 for ever. Only the space bar, at line 210, leaves.

records.d: 125PRINTTAB(14,19)"{&86}{&9D}{&84}< S >  {&9C}"TAB(4,21)"Press the space bar when you are"TAB(6,23)"happy with the sound level."

records.c: Lines 200-205: waits for a key until it is 0-5 or the space bar. A digit n sets S%=-3n, the SOUND loudness 0 (silent) to -15 (loudest) that the adventure uses for its sounds, and plays two short notes at that loudness (pitches 150 and 134, channels 1 and 2) so the player can hear it, then returns.

Lines 210-220, the space bar: A%=0, so that the adventure starts afresh, `Please wait.`, auto-repeat off (`*FX11,0`); level 0 also turns the MOS's sound off altogether (`*FX210,1`), which nothing on the disc turns on again. Then `*LOAD` the machine code CODE1/1 (to &0900) and CODE1/2 (to &0C00), and CHAIN"AD1".
Five zero bytes after the end mark, counted in the file's catalogue length of 631. BASIC never reads them.
